Ian looked at the frazzled student from across the jungle of houseplants on his desk.

"Everyone should have a hobby" Ian told her. "Even if you have really great goals for yourself - which you do. But we can get caught up in jumping through all the hoops it takes to get to our goals. That being said, that's a part of life and those individual steps are how you grow. The issue is perspective. If you take each step too seriously you end up stressing out over each one and you lose sight of how you're actually doing towards your goal. Don't get me wrong, stress has its advantages." Ian paused as he felt his phone vibrate. He slid it out to check who the message was from before continuing.

"I'm just worried that I'll come up short" the student told Ian. Ian nodded.

"How can you know what it takes to accomplish your goal when you haven't accomplished it yet? Stress prepares you for the worst by blowing things out of proportion: you're more motivated to complete a task if you're worried sick about it. So your stress isn't an accurate assessment of the situation. It's just your worst case scenario." The student nodded in agreement. Ian smiled as he watched her shoulder relax a little. Ian looked at his computer screen.

"You'll be fine. Everything you've turned in this semester has been excellent, and that's usually a really good indicator of how you'll do on the final. Her grades were great; better his grades when he had been in her position. He wrinkled his forehead in thought.

"Thanks" she said, grinning in mild embarrassment.

"I think the real reason you're so stressed out is that you're really invested in your goals here: I can tell that you really care about the subject matter. As you care about it and put effort towards it, it becomes a more critical part of your identity. You 'are' a good student. If you get a bad grade, that impacts your identity." Ian told her. Her brow furrowed as she processed the idea.

"This is good though! Knowing that is the key to reducing your stress: you can't let it become your entire identity. You have to be more than just a good student, say: a good student and a gardner. That way, if you get a bad grade, you can still say, 'at least I'm still a gardner'" he said, his eyes on his window. The room was dim and the morning cast hard rays of light through the blinds. He watched the dust appear and disappear as it floated down through the rays. The student looked up from the prayer plant on the corner of his desk she had been intently staring at.

"I am really into music." She admitted.

"How would you like a job DJ'ing a local radio station?" Ian asked.

"I mean... I've never done anything like that though" she said, staring down professor Ian's prayer plant.

"Oh that's fine!" Ian told her. "Jess knight is a good friend, she's in charge of scheduling. I'll shoot her an email and see if she can get you in to shadow her during a free slot."

"Thanks! Do you think that will help?"

"Absolutely, give it a shot. Make sure you keep exploring your hobbies though. All you have to do is ask. You never know what you'll find!" Ian said. The student got up started putting her backpack back on.

"Thanks again Professor Ian!"

"No problem Carley, I'll send you an email when I know more." Ian told her, leaning back in his chair. He watched as Carley left his office and closed the door behind her. The small room was quiet and still. It was dominated by book shelves that took up two adjacent walls that rose high above his desk, which drew one's attention to the fact that the room seemed taller than it was wide. Everything in the room was covered in a garden of odd plants ranging from venus flytraps to hanging vines suspended from the ceiling. The plants on the desk surrounded an old desktop computer, although a brand new tablet sat on top of stacks of folders and loose sheets of paper. He relaxed back into his seat, a comfy armchair that looked as if it had been rescued from a thrift store. He slid his phone back out to read the message he had received earlier.

"Wanna trip balls?"

Several years ago, a band I was in was playing a gig on Halloween night in a large club. We were popular around the area, it was a popular club, and the Halloween in question was on a Friday night, so it all stacked up to be the makings of a hell of a party. We showed up early, did our usual sound and light checks, and proceeded to chill out at the bar.

One of the bouncers there, whom we'll call Tim, was a friend of the band and a general all around likable guy. For a bouncer, he was small, but he was deceptively small and scrappy when he had to be. He showed up to work in his Halloween costume- a pencil-pushing nerd, complete with pocket protector.

A few minutes later, a group of guys came through the door, swaying, staggering, and laughing a little too loud for 8:00 pm. They'd obviously been pregaming quite a bit. One fella, we'll call him Drunk Dave, was particularly loud and boisterous. One look at him and it was obvious that his night was not going to end well.

Drunk Dave's first course of action was to slam back two Jagerbombs, and then ordered a round for his pals. The next thing he did was order two beers and began to double-fist it. Drunk Dave came to party. Tim, over in the corner, quietly kept an eye on him.

Now the music is playing and Drunk Dave makes his way to the floor, solo, except for his two beers. This is a no-no. This club has a "no drinks on the dance floor" policy. Drunk Dave clearly gives zero fucks. So he's out there drunkenly stagger-dancing to the music. Tim sees him and his alcoholic dance partners and has this look on his face like "Starting early tonight..." And goes out to the dance floor. He tells Drunk Dave to set his beers down at a table, and ol' Dave really had a problem with that. But he wasn't quiiiiite drunk enough to start a fight, so he agreed. However, as out nerdy-dressed bouncer walked away, Dave mocked him with a goofy walk and a stupid face as he walked away.

The real kicker started right at 9:00 though. This place was PACKED. We were about to take the stage and the club DJ was right in the middle of announcing us, and we were tuning up to start with our show opener (Queen's "Fat Bottomed Girls")

QUICKLY A NOTE about the club layout- the bar and dance floor were on the bottom level, and there was a balcony on the second floor where the DJ booth was, and it circled the whole dance floor and offered good viewing of the stage. It was killer.

Anyway, apparently Drunk Dave had made his way to the DJ Booth right at this moment and yanked the mic out of his hands and started drunkenly shouting something incoherently. Three things happened immediately-

1- Tim appeared like a ninja from the shadows directly next to Drunk Dave, and told him it was time to leave;

2- Drunk Dave, being right in front of the DJ booth, by virtue of this floor plan, was right in front of the balcony stairwell, and;

3- Drunk Dave REALLY didn't want to leave so he tried to punch Tim.

This led to Tim planting his foot right in the middle of Dave's chest and thrust-kicking him DOWN THE FUCKING STAIRS. He flipped end-over-end, takes a bounce, and then slides on his face to a halt in the middle of the dance floor.

Tim, in full nerd regalia, then decends the staircase and, in what would have been a blow to his pride has be been awake, drug Dave out to the parking lot to an awaiting police cruiser to the sound of thunderous applause.

It was a good night.
